description: Resolved handler definition, JSON-body kind and query-extractor kind per registered route. Generated from the real `.route(...)` surface; do not edit by hand.

counts_note.attribution: `derived` rows name a handler the parser resolved; `explicit` rows are pinned in EXPLICIT_ROUTE_HANDLERS (inline closures and paths served by two routers) and carry `attribution_note`.
counts_note.derived_tables: row counts of the three per-profile tables. `total` is their sum; `distinct` de-duplicates by (method, path). The gap is the two `/.well-known/{openid-configuration,jwks.json}` OIDC twins, which ship as an Always row plus an Oidc row.
counts_note.profile: marginal deployment profile per route, keys are the rendered `profile` lists ("" = default deployment). Derived from `Resolver.guards`, whose per-profile sets are cumulative (default ⊆ worker ⊆ all); a route in `all` but not `worker` needs the oidc-enabled router.
counts_note.query: per-route `Query<..>` extractor kind. `query_params` is populated for `typed` and `literal`; `literal` is a dynamic extractor whose key set is proven by string literals compared against the query key in the handler (or a same-file helper), while `opaque` (Value/HashMap with no such literal) and `foreign` (struct outside the scanned tree) have no addressable field list, and `ambiguous` includes every row whose handler cannot be named statically (the declared dynamic set).
counts_note.query_unknown: per-route serde policy for query names the extractor's struct does not declare: `reject` = `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` is on, so the name is a 400; `ignore` = serde drops it, so the call is a 200 with an unchanged result; `n/a` = no `Query<..>` extractor or no resolvable handler. `ignore` is a behaviour, not a decision — the routes that accept a documented foreign name on purpose are enumerated in `ledger_annotations.txt` as `query_ignored` and re-checked against the handler source, so this bucket can only shrink by fixing a handler or editing the ledger.
counts_note.routes: distinct (method, path) pairs this sidecar resolves; compare with status/confidence/body, which are per-route buckets.
counts_note.sdk_ledger: the SDK-side ledger is a cross-repo view and is intentionally not duplicated here — copying it would drift on every SDK change and turn this backend artifact into a mirror of another repository.

routes.attribution_note: inline closure registered inside create_router (server banner); no named fn exists to point at
builtin-oidc router serves `jwks`; `jwks_fallback` serves the same path from the fallback router when builtin OIDC is off
builtin-oidc router serves `openid_discovery`; `get_openid_configuration` is the fallback-router twin
